20. The reaction below shows a reaction at equilibrium.
   HCl(g)+NaOH (aq) ⇆ NaCl(aq)+H₂O(l)
   Find the equilibrium constant Kc and then analyze the direction which shift the reaction if their concentrations are [HCl]=3.2M [NaOH]=4.3m [NaCl]=6M and [H₂O]=2M
questions.answer_guide: Water is a pure liquid and is left out: Kc = [NaCl]/([HCl][NaOH]) = 6/(3.2 × 4.3) ≈ 0.44. Kc < 1, so reactants are favoured (lies to the left). (Including [H₂O] = 2 would give 0.87, not offered.) [Check against the official key.]

43. A sample gas occupies a volume of 1 liter at a pressure of 1 atm, At what pressure will its volume be 0.5 liter?(assuming temperature is constant) [ 4 marks]
   (Figure: piston with P = 1 atm, V = 1 L, T = 298 K compressed to V = 0.50 L, T = 298 K, P = ?)

questions.section: SECTION B: Structured Questions (60 Marks)
questions.question:
44. The table below which is collected at a set of temperature

   | Experiment | [A]    | [B]     | Rate     |
   | 1          | 0.20M  | 0.20M   | 0.4 M/s  |
   | 2          | 0.20 M | 0.040M  | 0.8 M/s  |
   | 3          | 0.40 M | 0.20M   | 1.6 M/s  |

  a) Determine the rate law? 3 marks
  b) Calculate the value of rate constant? 3 marks
questions.answer_guide:
Experiment 2's [B] is printed 0.040 M; it is evidently meant to be 0.40 M (doubling [B] doubles the rate).
a) Exp 1→3: [A] doubles, rate ×4 → second order in A. Exp 1→2: [B] doubles, rate ×2 → first order in B. Rate = k[A]²[B]
b) k = 0.4 / (0.20² × 0.20) = 0.4 / 0.008 = 50 M⁻²s⁻¹ [Check against the official key.]

questions.section: SECTION B: Structured Questions (60 Marks)
questions.question:
53. The following table shows the boiling points of alkanes, aldehydes, ketones and alcohols.

   | Name      | Structure       | Boiling point (°C) |
   | Pentane   | CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ | 36  |
   | Butanal   | CH₃CH₂CH₂CHO    | 76  |
   | 2-butane  | CH₃CH₂COCH₃     | 80  |
   | 1-butanol | CH₃CH₂CH₂CHOH   | 118 |

  a. Explain why aldehydes and ketones have lower boiling points than alcohols? 2 marks
  b. Predict which one has a higher boiling point pentane or butanal? Justify your answer. ? 2 marks
questions.answer_guide:
a. Alcohols form hydrogen bonds between molecules (O–H group); aldehydes and ketones cannot hydrogen-bond with each other and have only weaker dipole–dipole forces, so less energy is needed to boil them.
b. Butanal (76 °C) – its polar C=O group gives dipole–dipole attractions, which are stronger than the weak London (van der Waals) forces in non-polar pentane (36 °C).

questions.question: 55. The half life of the polonium - 210 is 138.4 days. How many milligrams of polonium -210 remains after 692 days if the starting with 8mg of isotope? 5marks
questions.answer_guide:
Number of half-lives = 692 / 138.4 = 5
Remaining = 8 × (½)⁵ = 8/32 = 0.25 mg
